_**User (2026-10-27 19:25:39Z)**_

Please come up with a plan to help me solve the following issue and answer the open questions:

The tag color editor must change when adding a custom HEX color. Firstly, if the user removes "#" from the beginning of their custom color, they cannot see the tag color dynamically change until they close the menu.
Additionally, when editing a custom HEX color, it should be easy to see the color that the tag is changing to. A custom color field should appear to the right of the HEX color text input, dynamically showing the custom color visually. The user should be able to easily see what color they are about to change their tag to without relying on looking at the small changes to the tag in the UI.

Acceptance Criteria
- The tag color editor should not allow "#" to be deleted in the text field.
- The tag color editor displays a dynamic preview of the user's custom color in a small box adjacent to the custom color text field.
- No tag coloring logic is broken.
Out of Scope
- A custom color editor
- Changes to the overall UI or structure of the color picker
- Changes to any tag logic
Open Questions
- What should the size of the color preview be, rectangle or square?
- Does this tag color picker appear elsewhere outside of editing tag colors?
- What is one non-trivial design decision that might need to be made either before or during implementation?

A new UI component will need to be created to dynamically render custom colors and some changes to the text field component will be needed. No backend changes are needed, and most color logic already exists.

import type { ChangeEvent, ReactNode } from 'react';
import {
  ColorPicker as AriaColorPicker,
  ColorSwatch as AriaColorSwatch,
  ColorSwatchPicker as AriaColorSwatchPicker,
  ColorField,
  ColorSwatchPickerItem,
  Dialog,
  DialogTrigger,
  parseColor,
} from 'react-aria-components';
import type {
  ColorPickerProps as AriaColorPickerProps,
  ColorSwatchProps,
} from 'react-aria-components';

import { css } from '@emotion/css';

import { Input } from './Input';
import { Popover } from './Popover';

function ColorSwatch(props: ColorSwatchProps) {
  return (
    <AriaColorSwatch
      {...props}
      style={({ color }) => ({
        background: color.toString('hex'),
        width: '32px',
        height: '32px',
        borderRadius: '4px',
        boxShadow: 'inset 0 0 0 1px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.1)',
      })}
    />
  );
}

const DEFAULT_COLOR_SET = [
  '#690CB0',
  '#D32F2F',
  '#C2185B',
  '#7B1FA2',
  '#512DA8',
  '#303F9F',
  '#1976D2',
  '#0288D1',
  '#0097A7',
  '#00796B',
  '#388E3C',
  '#689F38',
  '#AFB42B',
  '#FBC02D',
  '#FFA000',
  '#F57C00',
  '#E64A19',
  '#5D4037',
  '#616161',
  '#455A64',
  '#FF6666', //red
  '#FF99FF', //magenta
  '#C39DDF', //purple
  '#6666FF', //blue
  '#B2FFFF', //cyan
  '#99cb99', //green
  '#FFFF7F', //yellow
  '#FFAB66', //orange
  '#D4B89C', //brown
  '#BFBFBF', //gray
  '#FFAEAE', //colors repeat from above with a lighter tint
  '#FFCCFF',
  '#E4D4FF', //this is now purple125
  '#B0B0FF',
  '#D8FFFF',
  '#CFE5CF',
  '#FFFFB2',
  '#FFD5B3',
  '#E4D3C3',
  '#DADADA',
];

type ColorSwatchPickerProps = {
  columns?: number;
  colorset?: string[];
};

function ColorSwatchPicker({
  columns = 5,
  colorset = DEFAULT_COLOR_SET,
}: ColorSwatchPickerProps) {
  const pickers = [];

  for (let l = 0; l < colorset.length / columns; l++) {
    const pickerItems = [];

    for (let c = 0; c < columns; c++) {
      const color = colorset[columns * l + c];
      if (!color) {
        break;
      }

      pickerItems.push(
        <ColorSwatchPickerItem
          key={color}
          color={color}
          className={css({
            position: 'relative',
            outline: 'none',
            borderRadius: '4px',
            width: 'fit-content',
            forcedColorAdjust: 'none',
            cursor: 'pointer',

            '&[data-selected]::after': {
              content: '""',
              position: 'absolute',
              inset: 0,
              border: '2px solid black',
              outline: '2px solid white',
              outlineOffset: '-4px',
              borderRadius: 'inherit',
            },
          })}
        >
          <ColorSwatch />
        </ColorSwatchPickerItem>,
      );
    }

    pickers.push(
      <AriaColorSwatchPicker
        key={`colorset-${l}`}
        style={{
          display: 'flex',
          gap: '8px',
          flexWrap: 'wrap',
        }}
      >
        {pickerItems}
      </AriaColorSwatchPicker>,
    );
  }

  return pickers;
}
const isColor = (value: string) => /^#[0-9a-fA-F]{6}$/.test(value);

type ColorPickerProps = {
  children?: ReactNode;
  columns?: number;
  colorset?: string[];
} & AriaColorPickerProps;

export function ColorPicker({
  children,
  columns,
  colorset,
  ...props
}: ColorPickerProps) {
  const onInput = (value: string) => {
    if (!isColor(value)) {
      return;
    }

    const color = parseColor(value);
    if (color) {
      props.onChange?.(color);
    }
  };

  return (
    <AriaColorPicker defaultValue={props.defaultValue ?? '#690CB0'} {...props}>
      <DialogTrigger>
        {children}
        <Popover>
          <Dialog
            style={{
              outline: 'none',
              padding: '15px',
              display: 'flex',
              flexDirection: 'column',
              gap: '8px',
              minWidth: '192px',
              maxHeight: 'inherit',
              boxSizing: 'border-box',
              overflow: 'auto',
            }}
          >
            <ColorSwatchPicker columns={columns} colorset={colorset} />
            <ColorField
              onInput={({ target: { value } }: ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement>) =>
                onInput(value)
              }
            >
              <Input placeholder="#RRGGBB" style={{ width: '100px' }} />
            </ColorField>
          </Dialog>
        </Popover>
      </DialogTrigger>
    </AriaColorPicker>
  );
}

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-27 19:27:59Z)**_

I've written up a plan and answers to the three open questions. I haven't changed any code yet.

## Why the colour doesn't update without "#"

The picker is in [ColorPicker.tsx](packages/component-library/src/ColorPicker.tsx), in the shared component library. Two separate pieces of code handle the hex text field, and they disagree about the "#":

1. **Live updates while typing.** The local `onInput` handler only fires `onChange` if the text matches `isColor` ([ColorPicker.tsx:147](packages/component-library/src/ColorPicker.tsx#L147)), which requires a leading `#`. Typing `FF0000` fails that check, so nothing updates.
2. **Commit when the field loses focus.** react-aria's `ColorField` adds a `#` itself before parsing (`useColorFieldState`, line 61 in `react-stately`). So `FF0000` is only applied when the field blurs, which is usually when the popover closes.

That gap is exactly what the issue describes. The fix is small: make the "#" non-deletable, and that one change satisfies acceptance criterion 1 and removes the root cause.

## Plan

All changes are in `packages/component-library/src/`. The tag files and the backend don't change.

1. **Fix the hex input's handling of "#"** (see the design decision below for how).
   - Show a fixed `#` in front of an input that only accepts 6 hex characters (`maxLength={6}`, anything that isn't 0–9 or A–F is removed).
   - Before validating, rebuild the full value as `'#' + digits`. Then live updates work no matter what the user typed or pasted (including pasting `#FF0000`).
   - Change `isColor` to accept an optional leading `#`, so the check matches what `ColorField` already accepts.
2. **Add a new `ColorPreview` component** in its own file (`ColorPreview.tsx`), since the project rules say new components get their own file.
   - It takes a `color: string | null`, renders a small rounded box filled with that colour, and uses the same inset border shadow as `ColorSwatch` so light colours like `#FFFFB2` stay visible.
   - When there's no valid colour (a partial entry like `#FF0`), it shows an empty or checkerboard state rather than the last valid colour. That way the box always matches what's in the text field.
   - It gets an `aria-label` through `useTranslation` (for example, "Selected color preview") so screen readers get it and the i18n lint rule passes.
3. **Lay out the field and preview in one row.** Wrap the input and the preview in a horizontal `View` (`flexDirection: 'row'`, `gap: 8`, centred vertically). The swatch grid and popover stay as they are, which keeps the "overall structure" change out of scope.
4. **Keep the text field and preview in sync with swatch clicks.** Read the picker's current colour from `ColorPickerStateContext`, which `react-aria-components` 1.19 exports. Clicking a swatch then updates both the text and the preview.
5. **Tests and checks:**
   - Add a `ColorPicker.web.test.tsx` covering: "#" can't be removed (Backspace or select-all + Delete), typing 6 digits fires `onChange`, and the preview reflects what's typed. There are currently no tests for this component and no e2e tests for tags.
   - Add a Storybook story for the preview.
   - Run `yarn typecheck`, `yarn lint:fix` and `yarn test`.
   - The popover's appearance changes, so check for VRT snapshot diffs with the `running-vrts` skill.
   - Add a release note under `upcoming-release-notes/`.

## Open questions

**1. Should the preview be a rectangle or a square?**
A square, about 32×32px with a 4px corner radius. That is the same size as the swatches in the grid above it, so it reads as "this is the swatch you're making". 32px is also roughly the height of the `Input`, so the row lines up without adjusting heights. A wide rectangle would make the field and preview row wider than the 5-column grid (192px minimum) and could widen the popover, which goes against "no changes to overall UI structure".

**2. Does this picker appear anywhere outside tag colour editing?**
Not in the app today, but it's shared code. `ColorPicker` lives in the shared component library and is published as `@actual-app/components/color-picker`. Its only callers are:
- [TagEditor.tsx:22](packages/desktop-client/src/components/tags/TagEditor.tsx#L22), which recolours an existing tag from `TagRow` on the Manage Tags page.
- [TagCreationRow.tsx:167](packages/desktop-client/src/components/tags/TagCreationRow.tsx#L167), which picks a colour when creating a new tag.
- [ColorPicker.stories.tsx](packages/component-library/src/ColorPicker.stories.tsx), the Storybook stories.

So the change affects both the create and edit flows, which is desirable. Any future caller would get the new behaviour automatically, so the change should stay generic: nothing tag-specific in the component.

**3. A non-trivial design decision: how to make "#" impossible to delete.**
`ColorField` keeps the raw text in its own internal state, so we can't simply rewrite the input's value from outside. There are two approaches:

| | **A. Fixed "#" prefix, input holds 6 digits** (recommended) | **B. Keep "#" in the value and block deleting it** |
|---|---|---|
| How | Draw a `#` inside the input border; the input holds only the digits; use a controlled `Input` (or a controlled `ColorField`) | Intercept Backspace/Delete when the cursor is at position 1, plus select-all + delete, cut and paste, then put the `#` back and restore the cursor |
| Robustness | The `#` isn't in the text, so it can't be deleted | Easy to miss cases (IME input, cutting a selection, mobile keyboards); fights react-aria's internal state |
| Cost | Needs the swatch sync via `ColorPickerStateContext` (step 4) | Smaller diff, but more fragile |

I recommend A. A related decision to settle at the same time is whether the tag should keep updating on every valid keystroke. Today `TagEditor` calls `updateTag` (a database write) each time the input becomes a valid colour. With a live preview, a reasonable alternative is to update only the preview while typing and commit on blur or Enter. That avoids writing intermediate colours, but it's a behaviour change, so it needs a decision before implementation. "Changes to tag logic" are out of scope, so the default is to leave it as it is.

The repo recommends the `impeccable` design skill for UI work, but it isn't installed in this checkout. If you want a design pass on the preview box, run `npx impeccable install`.

import React from 'react';
import type {
  ChangeEvent,
  ComponentPropsWithRef,
  FocusEvent,
  KeyboardEvent,
} from 'react';
import { Input as ReactAriaInput } from 'react-aria-components';

import { css, cx } from '@emotion/css';

import { useResponsive } from './hooks/useResponsive';
import { styles } from './styles';
import { theme } from './theme';

export const baseInputStyle = {
  outline: 0,
  backgroundColor: theme.tableBackground,
  color: theme.formInputText,
  margin: 0,
  padding: 5,
  borderRadius: 4,
  border: '1px solid ' + theme.formInputBorder,
};

export const defaultInputClassName = css({
  ...baseInputStyle,
  color: theme.formInputText,
  whiteSpace: 'nowrap',
  overflow: 'hidden',
  flexShrink: 0,
  '&[data-focused]': {
    border: '1px solid ' + theme.formInputBorderSelected,
    boxShadow: '0 1px 1px ' + theme.formInputShadowSelected,
  },
  '&[data-disabled]': {
    color: theme.formInputTextPlaceholder,
  },
  '::placeholder': { color: theme.formInputTextPlaceholder },
  ...styles.smallText,
});

export type InputProps = ComponentPropsWithRef<typeof ReactAriaInput> & {
  onEnter?: (value: string, event: KeyboardEvent<HTMLInputElement>) => void;
  onEscape?: (value: string, event: KeyboardEvent<HTMLInputElement>) => void;
  onChangeValue?: (
    newValue: string,
    event: ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement>,
  ) => void;
  onUpdate?: (newValue: string, event: FocusEvent<HTMLInputElement>) => void;
};

export function Input({
  ref,
  onEnter,
  onEscape,
  onChangeValue,
  onUpdate,
  className,
  ...props
}: InputProps) {
  return (
    <ReactAriaInput
      ref={ref}
      className={
        typeof className === 'function'
          ? renderProps => cx(defaultInputClassName, className(renderProps))
          : cx(defaultInputClassName, className)
      }
      {...props}
      onKeyUp={e => {
        props.onKeyUp?.(e);

        if (e.key === 'Enter' && onEnter) {
          onEnter(e.currentTarget.value, e);
        }

        if (e.key === 'Escape' && onEscape) {
          onEscape(e.currentTarget.value, e);
        }
      }}
      onBlur={e => {
        onUpdate?.(e.currentTarget.value, e);
        props.onBlur?.(e);
      }}
      onChange={e => {
        onChangeValue?.(e.currentTarget.value, e);
        props.onChange?.(e);
      }}
    />
  );
}

const defaultBigInputClassName = css({
  padding: 10,
  fontSize: 'var(--font-size-15)',
  border: 'none',
  ...styles.shadow,
  '&[data-focused]': { border: 'none', ...styles.shadow },
});

export function BigInput({ className, ...props }: InputProps) {
  return (
    <Input
      {...props}
      className={
        typeof className === 'function'
          ? renderProps => cx(defaultBigInputClassName, className(renderProps))
          : cx(defaultBigInputClassName, className)
      }
    />
  );
}

export function ResponsiveInput(props: InputProps) {
  const { isNarrowWidth } = useResponsive();

  return isNarrowWidth ? <BigInput {...props} /> : <Input {...props} />;
}

import { fireEvent, render, screen } from '@testing-library/react';

import { Button } from './Button';
import { ColorPicker } from './ColorPicker';

function renderOpenPicker(defaultValue = '#690CB0') {
  const onChange = vi.fn();
  render(
    <ColorPicker defaultValue={defaultValue} onChange={onChange}>
      <Button>Pick a color</Button>
    </ColorPicker>,
  );
  fireEvent.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Pick a color' }));

  return {
    onChange,
    input: screen.getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Hex color' }),
    preview: () => screen.getByTestId('color-preview'),
  };
}

describe('ColorPicker', () => {
  it('shows the current color without "#" in the editable text', () => {
    const { input, preview } = renderOpenPicker('#690CB0');

    expect(input).toHaveProperty('value', '690CB0');
    expect(screen.getByText('#')).toBeTruthy();
    expect(preview().getAttribute('aria-label')).toBe(
      'Color preview: #690CB0',
    );
  });

  it('updates the color while typing, without needing "#"', () => {
    const { input, onChange, preview } = renderOpenPicker();

    fireEvent.change(input, { target: { value: 'FF0000' } });

    expect(onChange).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
    expect(onChange.mock.calls[0][0].toString('hex')).toBe('#FF0000');
    expect(preview().getAttribute('aria-label')).toBe(
      'Color preview: #FF0000',
    );
  });

  it('keeps the "#" prefix when all text is deleted', () => {
    const { input, onChange, preview } = renderOpenPicker();

    fireEvent.change(input, { target: { value: '' } });

    expect(input).toHaveProperty('value', '');
    expect(screen.getByText('#')).toBeTruthy();
    expect(onChange).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    expect(preview().getAttribute('aria-label')).toBe('No color preview');
  });

  it('strips "#" and invalid characters from pasted values', () => {
    const { input, onChange } = renderOpenPicker();

    fireEvent.change(input, { target: { value: '#00ff00zz' } });

    expect(input).toHaveProperty('value', '00ff00');
    expect(onChange.mock.calls[0][0].toString('hex')).toBe('#00FF00');
  });

  it('reverts an incomplete value on blur', () => {
    const { input, onChange, preview } = renderOpenPicker('#690CB0');

    fireEvent.change(input, { target: { value: 'FF0' } });
    expect(preview().getAttribute('aria-label')).toBe('No color preview');

    fireEvent.blur(input);

    expect(onChange).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    expect(input).toHaveProperty('value', '690CB0');
  });

  it('syncs the text and preview when a swatch is picked', () => {
    const { input, preview } = renderOpenPicker('#690CB0');

    fireEvent.click(screen.getByRole('option', { name: /D32F2F/i }));

    expect(input).toHaveProperty('value', 'D32F2F');
    expect(preview().getAttribute('aria-label')).toBe(
      'Color preview: #D32F2F',
    );
  });
});

# Writing Release Notes for actualbudget/actual

Release notes are the user-facing changelog. Each code change adds one Markdown file to `upcoming-release-notes/`, and these get collected into the published changelog at the next release. The authoritative source is the **Writing Good Release Notes** section of `packages/docs/docs/contributing/index.md`. Read it if anything below is unclear.

## The file

Create `upcoming-release-notes/<slug>.md`, where `<slug>` is a **short, descriptive kebab-case slug** naming the change (e.g. `add-payee-autocomplete.md`, `fix-mobile-category-delete.md`). Do **not** use a PR number, since the PR link is resolved automatically at release time. (Numeric filenames like `1234.md` still work, but a slug is preferred.)

```markdown
---
category: Features
authors: [YourGitHubUsername]
---

Add payee autocomplete to the transaction entry form
```

- **`category`**: exactly one of `Features` (new feature), `Enhancements` (improvement to an existing feature), `Bugfix` (bug fix), or `Maintenance` (internal change with no user-visible effect).
- **`authors`**: array of the GitHub username(s) who did the work.

## Writing the entry

The body is the changelog line. It is read by everyday users, not developers.

- **One sentence.** Short and clear. No paragraphs, no bullet lists, no long prose.
- **Plain language, no technical detail.** Describe what changed for the user, not how it was built. Avoid file names, function names, internal component names, and implementation jargon. (Exception: `Maintenance` entries may be technical, since they are for internal changes.)
- **Phrase it as a command.** Start with a present-tense verb: "Add …", "Fix …", "Show …", not "Added …" or "Adds …".
- Generally match the PR title, but reword it if that reads more clearly to a user.

Good: `Fix incorrect balance when reconciling an account with future transactions`
Too technical: `Fix off-by-one in reconcileTransactions() when txn.date > today`

## Decision needed: how to fix the broken links

The fix is to run `yarn install` inside the container, which recreates the links as `/workspaces/actual-budget/...` paths. I haven't done it, because this folder is shared with your Windows machine. Your `node_modules` was created from the Windows side, and reinstalling here would probably break it for tools you run on Windows (and rebuild native modules like `better-sqlite3` for Linux).

Options:
1. **Reinstall in the container**, if you do all your development inside the dev container. I'd then rerun typecheck and the full test suite.
2. **Run `yarn typecheck` and `yarn test` yourself on the Windows side**, where the links work.
3. **Skip it for now**, and let CI run typecheck when you open the PR.

**Also worth knowing:** after the lint run, `git status` shows about 280 unrelated files as modified, but none of them has a content change. It's a side effect of the formatter rewriting files on the shared WSL folder. I left them alone. When committing, only my 5 files should be staged:

# Running VRTs (Visual Regression Tests) in actualbudget/actual

VRTs are ordinary Playwright e2e tests in `packages/desktop-client/e2e/*.test.ts` that call:

```ts
await expect(target).toMatchThemeScreenshots();
```

`toMatchThemeScreenshots()` is a custom matcher defined in
`packages/desktop-client/e2e/fixtures.ts`. `target` is a `Page` or a `Locator` —
**prefer a tight locator** (e.g. a popover or panel) over the whole page to
reduce noise from charts and data.

## Key mechanics

- **No-op without `VRT=true`.** In a plain e2e run the matcher passes
  immediately, so `yarn workspace @actual-app/web run playwright test <file> -g "<name>"`
  verifies the interaction flow cheaply without needing snapshots — always do
  this first.
- **With `VRT=true`, each call captures three themes** (`auto` i.e. light,
  `dark`, `midnight`), producing numbered snapshots:
  `<file>.test.ts-snapshots/<Describe>-<test-name>-N-chromium-linux.png`.
  One test with 2 assertions → 6 PNGs.
- **Masking:** elements with `data-vrt-mask="true"` are masked out of
  screenshots. Use it for volatile content (real dates, version numbers).
- **Diff tolerance is strict:** `maxDiffPixels: 5`, `threshold: 0.05`
  (`packages/desktop-client/playwright.config.ts`).
- **Snapshots are Linux-only.** Committed snapshots end in
  `-chromium-linux.png` and must be generated inside the Playwright docker
  image. A host run on macOS writes `-chromium-darwin.png`, which CI ignores.

## Writing a new VRT

Import from the local fixtures, not `@playwright/test`:

```ts
import { expect, test } from './fixtures';
```

Patterns to copy:

- Date-picker popover VRT: `e2e/transactions.test.ts` ("by date").
- Report VRTs: `e2e/reports.test.ts`.
- Tests use the demo budget (`ConfigurationPage.createTestFile()`), whose data
  is pinned (date ranges show 2016), so snapshots are largely date-stable.
- Popovers render with a `[data-popover]` attribute — a good screenshot
  locator.
- Page models live in `e2e/page-models/`.

## Generating snapshots locally (docker)

Run all yarn commands from the repo root.

1. Start the dev server with HTTPS (background it; ready when
   `https://localhost:3001` returns 200 — `ignoreHTTPSErrors` is already set in
   the Playwright config):

   ```sh
   HTTPS=true yarn start
   ```

2. The container runs with `--network host`. On Linux it can reach
   `https://localhost:3001` directly. On macOS/Windows it cannot — get the
   machine's LAN IP (`ipconfig getifaddr en0` on macOS) and use
   `https://<LAN_IP>:3001` instead.

3. Run the Playwright docker image directly. The `bin/run-vrt` wrapper passes
   `-it`, which fails without a TTY, so in an agent shell invoke docker
   yourself:

   ```sh
   docker run --rm --network host -v "$(pwd)":/work/ -w /work/ \
     mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.61.1-jammy /bin/bash -c \
     "E2E_START_URL=https://<HOST>:3001 yarn vrt --update-snapshots -g '<test name>' <file>.test.ts"
   ```

   Pin the image tag to the repo's Playwright version (`@playwright/test` in
   `packages/desktop-client/package.json` — currently 1.61.1 →
   `v1.61.1-jammy`). The equivalent user-facing wrapper is
   `yarn vrt:docker --e2e-start-url https://<HOST>:3001 --update-snapshots`.

4. **Always scope `--update-snapshots`** with `-g`/file args to the new or
   changed test only — an unscoped update rewrites every screenshot in the
   repo.

5. Verify by re-running the exact same command **without**
   `--update-snapshots`; it must pass.

6. Optionally Read one generated PNG to sanity-check it shows the intended UI,
   then commit the test + PNGs (commit messages need the `[AI]` prefix — see
   the committing-actual-changes skill).

## Fallback without docker

Commit only the test file; CI generates the snapshots when someone comments
`/update-vrt` on the PR (`.github/workflows/vrt-update-generate.yml`).

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-28 20:33:30Z)**_

I'll answer the screenshot question now. The test results will follow when the run finishes.

## Test run status
- **Passed:** `ci-actions`, `cli`, `components` (this includes my 6 ColorPicker tests), `crdt`, `eslint-plugin-actual`.
- **Failed:** `api` and `web`. Lage only prints why after every package has finished, so I can't yet say whether these are real failures or the worker-startup timeouts we hit before. My change doesn't touch either package's code, but I won't claim that's the cause until I've read the output.
- **Still running:** `loot-core`, whose tests have been going for about an hour on this machine.

## How much work would a screenshot test be?

It would be more than "add one screenshot", because **the Manage Tags page has no e2e tests at all**. There's no page model for it in `e2e/page-models/` and no `tags.test.ts`. So the test would need:

1. **A page model** (`e2e/page-models/tags-page.ts`) with methods for: go to `/tags`, create a tag, open a tag's colour picker. Probably a navigation helper too. About 50–80 lines, modelled on `payees-page.ts`.
2. **A test file** (`e2e/tags.test.ts`) that loads the demo budget, creates a tag, opens the picker, types a hex value, and takes a screenshot of the popover (`[data-popover]`). About 40–60 lines. It would probably need to check whether the demo budget already has tags.
3. **Screenshots.** Each screenshot covers 3 themes, so 3–6 PNGs. They must be generated in the Linux Playwright Docker image, and Docker isn't available in this container. So you'd either run Docker on the host, comment `/update-vrt` on the PR, or use the `temp-update-vrt.yml` workflow pointed at this test.
4. **Checking for flakiness:** a popover with a text field and a live preview has to settle consistently before each screenshot.

That's roughly half a day to a day, mostly the page model, getting the test stable, and generating screenshots outside this container.

## Should it be a sub-issue?

Yes. A separate issue or follow-up is the better choice:
- **It isn't in the acceptance criteria.** The issue asks for the fixed "#", the preview and no broken tag logic. That's covered by the unit tests and your manual check.
- **The real gap is bigger than this feature.** The whole Manage Tags page (create, rename, delete, colour) has no e2e coverage. A follow-up titled "Add e2e coverage for Manage Tags" is more useful than a one-off screenshot attached to this PR.
- **It keeps this PR small** and doesn't make it wait on Docker or CI screenshot generation.

The repo rules don't let me create GitHub issues, but here's a draft for you to file:

> **Title:** Add e2e and VRT coverage for the Manage Tags page
>
> **Body:** The Manage Tags page (`/tags`) has no e2e tests or page model. Add a `tags-page.ts` page model and a `tags.test.ts` that covers creating a tag and changing its color, including a `toMatchThemeScreenshots()` VRT of the color picker popover (hex field with fixed `#` prefix and live color preview from #66). Snapshots must be generated in the Playwright docker image or via `/update-vrt`.

Once `yarn test` finishes, I'll read why `api` and `web` failed and report back.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-28 21:02:41Z)**_

That confirms it, and turned up a second problem. These are listed from biggest impact to smallest.

## 1. Move the repo off the Windows drive (by far the biggest win)

`/workspaces` is your Windows **C:\ drive, mounted into the container over `9p`/`drvfs`**. Every file read crosses from Linux into Windows and back, and that's very slow for what tests do: open thousands of small files in `node_modules` and the source. It explains everything we've seen this session:
- vitest workers timing out at startup ("Timeout waiting for worker to respond")
- a 4-minute run for a handful of component tests
- 7½ minutes to typecheck `desktop-client`
- `loot-core` tests running for 1½+ hours
- the broken `/mnt/host/c/...` links and the 777 permissions confusing `git status`

**Fix:** keep the repo on a Linux filesystem. Either:
- in VS Code, run **"Dev Containers: Clone Repository in Container Volume"**, which puts the code in a Docker volume, or
- clone it inside your WSL distro (e.g. `~/actual-budget`) and open the dev container from there.

Native Linux file access is often 5–10× faster for workloads like this. Once on a Linux filesystem, do a fresh `yarn install` there, which also gets rid of the link workaround I made.

## 2. Free up space on C: (urgent regardless)

**Your C: drive is 98% full: only 5.2 GB free out of 238 GB.** Windows slows down noticeably when that full, and builds, test caches and Docker images (the Playwright image alone is ~2 GB) could run out of space entirely. Clearing space helps now, and you'll need it for step 1 anyway, since Docker volumes and WSL disks are stored on C: by default.

## 3. Don't run the dev server during tests

`yarn start` is still running three Vite processes, two of them watching for file changes. On this slow mount, file-watching alone is expensive, and it competes for CPU with the test workers. I'd stop it before rerunning tests. Since your manual check is done, I can stop it now.

## 4. Exclude the repo from Windows Defender

While the repo stays on C:, real-time antivirus scanning checks every file that tests and builds open. Adding the repo folder (`C:\Users\icsab\actual-budget`) to Defender's exclusions usually helps noticeably. Only do this if your school or organisation's policy allows it.

## 5. Run less

- **Test only what you changed:** `yarn workspace @actual-app/components run test` takes minutes, where the full `yarn test` takes hours. CI runs everything anyway.
- **Let lage's cache work:** `yarn test` (not `yarn test:debug`) skips packages whose files haven't changed since a passing run, so reruns are much faster. Only clear `.lage/` if results look stale.

## 6. Give WSL more resources (minor)

The container sees 12 cores and about 7.8 GB of RAM, which is adequate. If you have more RAM, you can raise WSL's limit in `%UserProfile%\.wslconfig` (e.g. `memory=12GB`). This helps much less than step 1.

One thing I'd **not** change: vitest suggested sharing the test environment across files (`pool: 'vmThreads'` / `isolate: false`). That's a config change to the repo itself that could make tests interfere with each other, and it doesn't address the real cause, the slow file access.

Do you want me to stop the dev server now, so the rest of `yarn test` runs faster?

## Why `api`, `web` and `core` failed

I checked the error for every failing test (28 in total). Except for one, they all failed because a test or its setup ran out of time:

The "database connection is not open" messages in the log are a knock-on effect: a setup step times out, the database is closed, and the next test can't use it. Four of the failing tests are in "Tags" groups, but they test the API's tag database functions, which have nothing to do with the colour picker. The other tag tests in the same file passed.
- **`web`**: 7 `TransactionsTable` tests hit "Test timed out in 10000ms". Its second test run (the one that reported "no tests") never started, because every one of its test files hit the worker-startup timeout.

That's a temporary test folder colliding with a leftover copy during the slow run. The folder is gitignored and gone now, so it was a one-off.

Base directory for this skill: /workspaces/actual-budget/.claude/skills/committing-actual-changes

# Committing Changes in actualbudget/actual

Before creating any git commit or pull request in this repo, read:

**`.github/agents/pr-and-commit-rules.md`**

It is the authoritative source for the rules you must apply yourself: the `[AI]` PR-title prefix and leaving the PR template blank (and the Chinese exception). The mechanical commit/git rules are enforced by tooling and aren't restated there. Read it on every commit/PR session so any updates are picked up automatically.

## The one rule worth restating

Every commit message and every pull request title MUST begin with `[AI]`. Commit messages are checked by the git-guard hook (a missing prefix is blocked before the commit lands), so the one that needs _your_ attention is the PR title — nothing checks it for you, and the cost of forgetting it is high since the PR has to be renamed by hand. Examples:

- `[AI] Fix type error in account validation` — correct
- `Fix type error in account validation` — wrong, missing prefix

The PR-template rule and the rest live in the rules file. Read it before each commit/PR rather than relying on this skill's summary, because the rules file evolves and this skill deliberately does not restate it.

## Why this matters

Maintainers triage AI-authored contributions separately, and the `[AI]` prefix is what makes that triage fast — it also drives the automatic `"AI generated"` PR label, so getting the prefix right is the one action that gates the whole triage path. Without it the PR looks like a normal human contribution and the wrong review process gets applied. The "do not fill in the PR template" rule exists because the human is the one who actually tested the change and can write the Description / Testing / Checklist sections honestly — an AI-filled template misrepresents who did what.

The rules file is short. Read it.
